title: Committed-input admission refuses evaluation when the item's own acceptance needs a deliberately failing run as the newest result
outcome: An item whose acceptance requires a deliberately failing test run can be evaluated without having to bury that run under a later passing one, for example by letting its criteria name the intended fail run so admission does not treat it as the newest applicable result.
acceptance: A design note on this item states how an item's criteria can name an intended failing run (or otherwise exempt it), and how committed-input admission then chooses the applicable terminal result, with the owner's or coordinator's concurrence recorded.

If implemented, a behavioral regression shows admission accepting an evaluation whose newest terminal result on the named root's HEAD is a named intended-fail run, and still refusing when an un-named failing run is newest.
